sections.heading: Bottom-up estimates
sections.markdown:
**Unit economics, FY2025 actuals ($B, yfinance XOM income/cashflow).** Revenue 323.9; NI 28.84 (EPS $6.70); CFO 51.97; capex 28.36 → FCF 23.61. DDA 25.99 → CFO/NI 1.80x. Q2-2026 (XOM IR release 2026-07-31): GAAP earnings $14.5B, CFO $23.6B, cash capex $6.8B → FCF ~$17B in a single war-premium quarter; production 4,514 koebd, "highest upstream production in more than two decades"; Permian "more than 1.8 Moebd"; Guyana 5th FPSO startup on plan 4Q26 (+250 Kbd).

**Committed estimate.** FY2026E NI ~$42–46B (H1-26 actual $18.7B at yfinance; H2 at ~Q2 run-rate with Brent ~96 held), EPS ~$10–11. FY2028E NI ~$45–50B, EPS ~$11.5–12.5 at ~$90 Brent: volume ~+3%/yr plus share count shrinking ~2%/yr on the ~$20B buyback. Through-cycle stress (FY2025-caliber, sub-$80 Brent): FCF ~$24B covers the $17.2B dividend 1.37x.

**Load-bearing assumptions (each cited):**
1. **Price deck**: Brent ≈95.85 with the war premium intact (the macro regime memo 2026-09-05: "Brent ≈95.85 ... the Hormuz/Gulf war premium that drove the re-rate is intact"). Underwrite centered ~95–96; stress to FY2025 sub-$80 realized economics.
2. **Volume growth**: Permian "record ... more than 1.8 Moebd, consistent with planned 9% CAGR through 2030"; Guyana 5th FPSO "startup on plan for 4Q26, increasing capacity by 250 Kbd"; total 4,514 koebd (Q2-2026 release). Model total ~+3%/yr to ~5.0M boe/d by 2029.
3. **Capital-return durability**: Q3-26 dividend declared $1.03/share payable 2026-09-10; $5.1B buybacks in Q2-26 (~$20B/yr) (Q2-2026 release). FY25 FCF 23.61 vs dividends 17.23 (yfinance) — 1.37x cover in the weakest cash year of the window; capex stays ~$28–30B/yr (FY25 28.36 yfinance; $13.0B YTD-26 per Q2 release).

Uncited load-bearing assumption: none — all three sourced above.

sections.heading: Priors disclosure
sections.markdown: From memory the market narrative is that XOM is a best-in-class integrated major whose Permian/Guyana growth and ≥$30B capital-return program justify a premium to the E&P pack, while spot ~$95 Brent is treated as war-premium windfall that will reverse — the question is whether the equity already prices that windfall.

sections.heading: Base-rate anchoring
sections.markdown: Primary prior is **commodity_capex_turnaround** (the base-rate library: 0.42, +75/-35, 3y). I anchor p_up at **0.45** (+3pp): the delivered growth (production already the highest in two decades) and a $31.8B-net-debt / $259B-equity fortress raise the work-rate modestly above the registry, but entry at ~14x war-premium forward earnings is not a trough buy, so I hold the deviation small and keep down_pct at the full -35 registry (XOM fell >35% in prior Brent busts despite an uncut dividend — the dividend does NOT truncate the price tail). The **dividend_income_anchor** (0.60, +25/-15) does not govern the prior: at 2.6% gross yield XOM is not a yield-capture name, but its never-cut dividend is the downside cushion inside the -35 losing mean.

sections.heading: Variant perception
sections.markdown:
**Market believes:** The ~$159 price capitalizes ~$95 war-premium earnings as ephemeral; a Brent normalization to ~$70 knocks XOM back to ~$110–120, the buyback gets cut, and the energy complex should be avoided until the premium clears — hence the macro desk's NEUTRAL bloc stance and the market's refusal to pay growth multiples for oil.

**Why wrong:** The market models XOM as spot-Brent × static barrels, underweighting the **per-share floor that rises each year regardless of Brent**: low-cost volumes already delivered (Permian 9% CAGR to 2030, Guyana +250 Kbd in 4Q26) and ~$20B/yr of buybacks shrink the count ~2%/yr, so EPS compounds ~5%/yr at a *constant* oil price. The dividend is not the risk the market prices: it was covered 1.37x by FCF in the weakest cash year of the window (FY25) and XOM has not cut it in 40+ years; the flexible buyback — not the dividend — is the shock absorber in a downturn. At ~14x FY26E and ~10x through-cycle EBITDA, the equity prices the windfall but not the compounding, and a fortress balance sheet means the "Brent collapses and the dividend breaks" tail the market leans on has no balance-sheet mechanism behind it.

**What proves us wrong:** Brent durably below ~$81.5 (macro review marker), a dividend cut, a Permian decline or Guyana FPSO slip, or a buyback suspension that reveals the program was not FCF-durable.

**Edge taxonomy:** analytical (market mis-models the mechanism — static-barrel spot framing ignores the volume + buyback per-share floor) + time-arbitrage (3y compounding view through an event-by-event Brent tape). Factor diversification (oil_gas absent from the GLOBAL card) is a portfolio role, not the edge.

sections.heading: Disconfirming facts
sections.markdown:
1. Quarterly dividend declared $1.03/share payable 2026-09-10 (Q2-2026 IR release) — any cut below this invalidates the floor.
2. FY2025 FCF $23.61B vs dividends $17.23B = 1.37x cover in the window's weakest cash year (yfinance cashflow); a quarter printing FCF below the dividend is the first crack.
3. Permian "more than 1.8 Moebd" with planned 9% CAGR through 2030; Guyana 5th FPSO on plan for 4Q26 (Q2-2026 release) — a startup slip or decline breaks the growth leg.
4. Brent reference 95.9 with ±15% marker band lower bound ~81.5 (the macro regime memo markers) — a sustained sub-$81.5 close removes the war-premium premise.
5. $5.1B buyback in Q2-26 (Q2-2026 release); a formal suspension — beyond a pace cut — shows the program is not FCF-durable.

sections.heading: Pre-mortem
sections.markdown: It is late 2029 and this position lost ~30%. The most likely reason: the war premium fully repriced — Brent to ~$70, XOM EPS to ~$8, multiple to ~13x, price ~$110. The dividend survived (it was never the risk), but the buyback pause removed the per-share support and the sector "quality" premium deflated with it. Second joint: I paid ~14x war-premium forward earnings with only a +3pp p_up deviation — a no-margin-of-safety entry whose EV (+2.8%) rests on the premium persisting; when it did not, the -35 tail dominated.

sections.heading: Earnings-quality gate
sections.markdown: Accruals (NI−CFO)/avg assets: FY23 −5.19%, FY24 −5.14%, FY25 −5.13% — consistently negative, cash structurally above NI (D&A ~$26B). Cash conversion CFO/NI 1.80x. Divergence flags: FY25 receivables +2.0% and inventory +11.8% against revenue −4.5% and COGS −3.7% — price-cycle working capital, optics-class only (working capital absorbed ~$7.3B in FY25). Related-party: none (US major). IDX regime/notation: N/A. Structure flags: none — low leverage ($31.8B net debt vs $259B equity at 2Q26). No manipulation-class flag; no estimate haircut required, noted for pre-mortem.

sections.heading: Bear attack
sections.markdown:
(Drew appends verbatim; survives the Judge verdict — never edited by a later stage)

1. **Sub-hurdle by your own numbers.** ev_math replicates +2.8% total/3y ≈ +0.9%/yr vs 3.63% risk-free (macro_regime fed_path) and the house hurdle (BOND_FR_MATH: equity return must exceed FR carry by ~4%/yr). ~2.7pp below risk-free with catalyst_date null — not fundable even if every estimate is right.
2. **Archetype misapplied; deviation faces the wrong way.** commodity_capex_turnaround wins on "capex down, projects deferred" (the base-rate library). XOM is the inverse: $28–30B capex rising, Guyana 5th FPSO, Permian 9% CAGR — a peak-margin buy at ~14–15x war-premium forward EPS, the archetype's named dominant failure ("low P/E at peak-margin, incentive-price trap"). Honest p_up is below 0.42, not 0.45. up_pct capped at +35 vs base +75: the trade keeps the archetype's −35 tail without its +75 win.
3. **Down tail understated; the dividend doesn't truncate it.** Kill 104 = −35%, and it's "NOT a stop" — the position rides the collapse. 2020: XOM ≈ −55% peak-to-trough, dividend never cut (yfinance 2020); you concede price tails aren't truncated, yet commit −35. At honest −45: 0.45·35 + 0.55·(−45) + 6.6 − 0.3 = −2.7%. Fragile — single-assumption dependency.
4. **Buyback double-counted.** The ~2%/yr share shrink compounds EPS only in the up state; the same buyback is the downturn "shock absorber," cut first when Brent falls. The "floor that rises regardless of Brent" runs on ~$95 FCF — circular. ~$20B/yr repurchases at 14–15x peak-cycle EPS is value-destructive timing, not compounding.
5. **Kill criteria contradict the stated invalidation.** Thesis is "dead durably below ~$81.5" (What proves us wrong), yet the Brent kill only triggers review at <$65 — 16 points below the macro ±15% full-rebuild trip (band floor 81.5). Between 81.5 and 65 the equity de-rates ~25% with no exit.
6. **Disconfirming fact:** the macro desk says "geopolitics overlay — underwrite name-by-name, do not chase" (macro_regime tilts). Buying $159 on the intact premium is that forbidden chase; pricing the windfall as ephemeral is correct compensation, not mispricing.
7. **Pre-mortem is the base case.** Your 2029 post-mortem (Brent→$70, −30%) is the modal path — war premiums faded in 2022 and 2023. Funded −35% coin flip, zero excess return, no stop, no catalyst, sizing null.

**Re-attack (2026-09-05).** The Revision's concession is honest and complete: every numbered point is answered, all moves against the trade, none requiring a new-evidence raise. Arithmetic reconciles — 0.40×35 + 0.60×−45 + 6.6 − 0.3 = −6.7 exactly. Frontmatter coheres: kill 88 < entry 159.47 < target 216; |down_pct| = (159.47−88)/159.47 = 44.8% ≈ 45; up_pct 35 vs (216−159.47)/159.47 = 35.5% — both inside lint band; kill_criteria notes match the moved levels (price kill ~−45%, brent 81.5 = the macro ±15% band floor). Nothing is left undefended, and nothing is overstated: −6.7% expected is negative at every size. Quarter-Kelly on a −6.7% EV is zero; no scaling rescues a sub-hurdle, catalyst-free, sub-registry thesis. At ~−2.2%/yr it is ~6pp below the 3.63% risk-free and the ~4%/yr house equity-premium hurdle (the fund rules / the base-rate library fr_duration_carry). Sizing stays null; the analyst already recommends zero. Shelving is Aldrich's call — as underwritten this entry is un-fundable. **FINAL VERDICT: KILL_RECOMMENDED.**

sections.heading: Revision
sections.markdown:
(Sloane, 2026-09-05. All moves are against the trade; no new evidence cited.)

1. Concede. +2.8%/3y ≈ +0.9%/yr beats neither 3.63% risk-free nor the ~4%/yr equity-premium hurdle; sub-hurdle and catalyst-free, unfundable even if estimates hold.

2. Concede. Rising-capex mid-upturn, not a capex-down turnaround: the archetype's dominant failure. The +3pp deviation faced the wrong way; p_up cut 0.45→0.40, below the 0.42 registry (base_rate.source updated). up_pct held at +35, which is target math, not the base +75 win.

3. Concede. 2020 printed ≈ −55% peak-to-trough with the dividend uncut; the −35 kill is no risk stop. down_pct widened to −45 and the price kill realigned to ~88 (−45%) so ev_math matches the honest losing mean. At 0.40/−45, EV −6.7%, negative.

4. Concede in part. Buyback-as-floor is circular: it runs on ~$95 FCF and is cut first in a bust. Retired shares persist, but at 14–15x peak-cycle EPS the accretion is thin; per-share growth is Brent-conditional.

5. Concede and fix. brent_12m review trigger raised 65→81.5, the macro ±15% band floor, matching my stated invalidation line (kill_criteria updated).

6. Concede in part. Name-by-name, not bloc-chasing, so the tilt's letter is met; but $159 embeds the intact war premium the desk treats as overlay. Ephemeral pricing is compensation, not mispricing, at this level.

7. Concede. Pre-mortem is the modal path; 2022/23 war premiums faded. Honest EV negative, sub-hurdle, no catalyst, no stop. Recommend zero size; kill or shelve until a trough entry restores margin of safety.

sections.heading: Judge verdict
sections.markdown:
Calibration: commodity_capex_turnaround has zero own-book GLOBAL cases in the kill ledger (n_own < 10), so the 0.42 registry prior stands unblended — no calibration history supports another look at this entry. The base-rate honesty is real: p_up 0.40 below the 0.42 registry is a correct downward deviation. But it was forced by conceding the archetype was misapplied, and shading does not rescue negative economics.

VERDICT: KILL — reason_tag valuation. (1) Drew's final kill survives my restatement: EV = 0.40×35 + 0.60×−45 + 6.6 − 0.3 = −6.7%/3y ≈ −2.2%/yr against 3.63% risk-free and the ~4%/yr house equity-premium hurdle — negative excess at every size, quarter-Kelly zero, catalyst null. A negative-EV trade has no fundable fraction, so PASS_REDUCED is unavailable. (2) The analyst conceded all seven points with every move against the trade and recommends zero — no defense stands that I could credit beyond the concession. (3) XOM's claimed edge — low-cost Permian/Guyana growth, uncut dividend, buyback — is itself the cyclical mechanism, not a structural franchise: entry at ~14x peak war-premium forward EPS with capex rising is the archetype's named dominant failure (incentive-price trap), unlike the genuine WeChat moat that justified PASS_REDUCED in 0700HK. (4) Entry $159.47 carries no margin of safety to the $88 thesis-invalidating kill (−45%); the analyst's own pre-mortem (Brent→$70, −30%) is the modal path. Shelving until a trough entry restores margin of safety is the correct disposition, but shelving is not a fundable position.
